description: Constrained and unconstrained nonlinear solvers, linear/quadratic/integer programming, least-squares solvers, the problem-based modelling API, and global and derivative-free optimization methods.

tools.name: fmincon
tools.description: Find a local minimum of a nonlinear multivariable function subject to bounds, linear equality/inequality constraints and nonlinear constraints. Four algorithms are available, with 'interior-point' the robust default and 'sqp' often faster for smooth, small problems. Supplying analytic gradients through options dramatically improves speed and reliability.
tools.usage:
x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b)
x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, lambda, grad, hessian] = fmincon(___)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Objective function handle; returns [f, gradf] when SpecifyObjectiveGradient is true.

parameters.name: x0
parameters.description: Initial point; the solver finds only a local minimum near it.

parameters.name: A, b, Aeq, beq
parameters.description: Linear inequality (A*x <= b) and equality (Aeq*x = beq) constraints.

parameters.name: lb, ub
parameters.description: Lower and upper bounds; use -Inf/Inf where unbounded.

parameters.name: nonlcon
parameters.description: Handle returning [c, ceq] with c <= 0 and ceq = 0.

tools.notes: Always check exitflag: positive means converged. Use multiple starting points (MultiStart) if the problem is nonconvex.

tools.name: fminunc
tools.description: Find a local minimum of an unconstrained nonlinear function using quasi-Newton or trust-region methods. The trust-region algorithm requires a user-supplied gradient but converges much faster on large, smooth problems. Use it whenever there are genuinely no constraints; with bounds only, use fmincon or fminbnd.
tools.usage:
x = fminunc(fun, x0)
x = fminunc(fun, x0, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, grad, hessian] = fminunc(___)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Objective handle; return [f, g] (and optionally the Hessian) when the corresponding options are set.

parameters.name: 'SpecifyObjectiveGradient'
parameters.description: Logical; true when fun returns the gradient.

tools.notes: For nonsmooth objectives use fminsearch (Nelder-Mead) or patternsearch instead.

tools.name: fminsearch
tools.description: Minimize an unconstrained multivariable function using the derivative-free Nelder-Mead simplex algorithm. It needs no gradients and tolerates mildly nonsmooth or noisy objectives, but converges slowly and is unreliable above roughly ten variables. It ships with base MATLAB and needs no toolbox licence.
tools.usage:
x = fminsearch(fun, x0)
x = fminsearch(fun, x0, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output] = fminsearch(___)
tools.notes: Uses optimset, not optimoptions, because it is a base MATLAB function.

tools.name: linprog
tools.description: Solve a linear programming problem: minimize f'*x subject to linear inequality, equality and bound constraints. The dual-simplex algorithm is the default and is usually both fast and numerically robust. Returns the optimal point, objective value, exit flag and Lagrange multipliers for sensitivity analysis.
tools.usage:
x = linprog(f, A, b)
x = linprog(f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, lambda] = linprog(___, options)

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Coefficient vector of the linear objective (minimized).

tools.notes: linprog always minimizes; negate the objective to maximize. lambda.ineqlin gives shadow prices.

tools.name: intlinprog
tools.description: Solve a mixed-integer linear program, where some variables are restricted to integer values. It uses branch-and-bound with cutting planes and heuristics, and reports the relative gap between the incumbent solution and the best bound. Use it for scheduling, assignment, knapsack and facility-location problems.
tools.usage:
x = intlinprog(f, intcon, A, b)
x = intlinprog(f, intcon, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
[x, fval, exitflag, output] = intlinprog(___, options)

parameters.name: intcon
parameters.description: Indices of the variables constrained to be integers.

parameters.name: f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub
'RelativeGapTolerance'
parameters.description: Stop when the optimality gap is below this fraction.

parameters.name: 'IntegerTolerance'
parameters.description: How close to an integer a value must be to count as integral.

tools.name: quadprog
tools.description: Solve a quadratic programming problem: minimize 0.5*x'*H*x + f'*x subject to linear constraints. When H is positive semidefinite the problem is convex and the solution is a global minimum. It underpins portfolio optimization, model predictive control and SVM training.
tools.usage:
x = quadprog(H, f)
x = quadprog(H, f, A, b)
x = quadprog(H, f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, x0, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, lambda] = quadprog(___)

parameters.name: H
parameters.description: Symmetric Hessian matrix of the quadratic term.

parameters.name: A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub

tools.notes: Note the factor of 1/2 in the objective: pass H = 2*Sigma to minimize x'*Sigma*x.

tools.name: lsqnonlin
tools.description: Solve nonlinear least-squares problems by minimizing the sum of squares of a vector-valued residual function, with optional bounds and constraints. Because you return the residual vector rather than the scalar sum, the solver can exploit the Gauss-Newton structure. It is the right solver for model calibration and data fitting.
tools.usage:
x = lsqnonlin(fun, x0)
x = lsqnonlin(fun, x0, lb, ub)
x = lsqnonlin(fun, x0, lb, ub, options)
[x, resnorm, residual, exitflag, output, lambda, jacobian] = lsqnonlin(___)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Handle returning the residual VECTOR, not its sum of squares.

parameters.name: 'SpecifyObjectiveGradient'
parameters.description: True when fun also returns the Jacobian.

parameters.name: 'FiniteDifferenceType'
parameters.description: 'forward' (default) or 'central' for more accurate numeric derivatives.

tools.notes: A common error is returning sum(r.^2); return r itself.

tools.name: lsqcurvefit
tools.description: Fit a parameterized model to data in the least-squares sense, taking the model function, x data and y data separately. It is a convenience wrapper around lsqnonlin that forms the residual for you. Bounds on the parameters are supported, which makes it useful for physically constrained fits.
tools.usage:
x = lsqcurvefit(fun, x0, xdata, ydata)
x = lsqcurvefit(fun, x0, xdata, ydata, lb, ub)
[x, resnorm, residual, exitflag, output, lambda, jacobian] = lsqcurvefit(___, options)

parameters.name: xdata, ydata
parameters.description: Independent and dependent data, matching sizes.

tools.name: lsqlin
tools.description: Solve a linearly constrained linear least-squares problem: minimize ||C*x - d|| subject to linear inequality, equality and bound constraints. It is the constrained generalization of the backslash operator. Use it for regularized or physically constrained regression such as nonnegative or sum-to-one coefficients.
tools.usage:
x = lsqlin(C, d, A, b)
x = lsqlin(C, d, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
[x, resnorm, residual, exitflag, output, lambda] = lsqlin(___, x0, options)

parameters.name: C, d
parameters.description: Design matrix and observation vector of the least-squares objective.

tools.name: lsqnonneg
tools.description: Solve the nonnegative least-squares problem, minimizing ||C*x - d|| subject to x >= 0, using the classic Lawson-Hanson active-set algorithm. Nonnegativity is often the only constraint needed for spectral unmixing, deconvolution and mixture estimation. It ships with base MATLAB.
tools.usage:
x = lsqnonneg(C, d)
[x, resnorm, residual, exitflag, output, lambda] = lsqnonneg(C, d, options)

tools.name: fsolve
tools.description: Solve a system of nonlinear equations F(x) = 0 starting from an initial guess. Three algorithms are available; 'trust-region-dogleg' is the default for square systems and 'levenberg-marquardt' is more forgiving of poor starting points. Providing the Jacobian through options greatly improves speed and robustness.
tools.usage:
x = fsolve(fun, x0)
x = fsolve(fun, x0, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, jacobian] = fsolve(___)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Handle returning the residual vector F(x) (and optionally the Jacobian).

parameters.name: 'SpecifyObjectiveGradient'
parameters.description: True when fun returns the Jacobian.

tools.notes: exitflag > 0 means converged; a small ||F|| is not by itself proof of a root for badly scaled systems.

tools.name: fminimax
tools.description: Minimize the worst-case (maximum) value of a set of objective functions subject to constraints. This minimax formulation is used for robust design, equiripple filter design and Chebyshev approximation. Constraints are specified exactly as for fmincon.
tools.usage:
x = fminimax(fun, x0)
x = fminimax(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
[x, fval, maxfval, exitflag, output, lambda] = fminimax(___, nonlcon, options)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Handle returning a VECTOR of objective values; the maximum is minimized.

parameters.name: A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon
'AbsoluteMaxObjectiveCount'
parameters.description: Number of leading objectives whose absolute value is minimized.

tools.name: fgoalattain
tools.description: Solve a multiobjective goal-attainment problem: find the design that comes closest to a set of goals, with relative under- or over-achievement controlled by weights. It converts a multiobjective problem into a single parameterized scalar problem. Use it for controller and filter design with competing specifications.
tools.usage:
x = fgoalattain(fun, x0, goal, weight)
x = fgoalattain(fun, x0, goal, weight, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, options)
[x, fval, attainfactor, exitflag, output, lambda] = fgoalattain(___)

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: Relative importance / trade-off weights; commonly abs(goal).

parameters.name: attainfactor
parameters.description: Negative means all goals are over-achieved, positive means under-achieved.

tools.name: optimoptions
tools.description: Create or modify an options object for a specific solver, with validation and tab-completion of only the options that solver supports. It replaces the older optimset for all Optimization Toolbox and Global Optimization Toolbox solvers. Display it to see every option and its current value.
tools.usage:
options = optimoptions(SolverName)
options = optimoptions(SolverName, Name, Value, ...)
options = optimoptions(oldoptions, Name, Value)
options = optimoptions(prob)

parameters.name: 'PlotFcn' / 'OutputFcn'
parameters.description: Live plots or custom callbacks during the solve.

parameters.name: 'UseParallel'
parameters.description: Logical; parallelize finite-difference gradients or population evaluation.

tools.example:
opts = optimoptions('fmincon', ...
    'Algorithm', 'interior-point', ...
    'Display', 'iter-detailed', ...
    'MaxFunctionEvaluations', 5000, ...
    'OptimalityTolerance', 1e-10, ...
    'PlotFcn', {@optimplotfval, @optimplotstepsize});
x = fmincon(@(x) sum(x.^2), [1 1], [], [], [], [], [-5 -5], [5 5], [], opts);

tools.name: optimproblem
tools.description: Create an optimization problem object for the problem-based workflow, where you write the objective and constraints as algebraic expressions in optimization variables. MATLAB then chooses a suitable solver and translates the model automatically. This is far more readable and less error-prone than assembling matrices by hand.

parameters.name: 'Objective'
parameters.description: An optimization expression built from optimvar variables.

parameters.name: 'Constraints'
parameters.description: Structure of named constraint expressions or arrays.

tools.notes: Use prob2struct to inspect the matrices MATLAB generates, or to hand them to a solver directly.

tools.name: optimvar
tools.description: Create an optimization variable (scalar, vector, matrix or indexed by strings) for use in the problem-based workflow. Bounds and the variable type (continuous or integer) are set at creation. Named index sets make models that mirror the real problem structure.
tools.usage:
x = optimvar(name)
x = optimvar(name, n)
x = optimvar(name, m, n, Name, Value)
x = optimvar(name, indexNames, Name, Value)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Variable name used in displays and in the solution structure.

parameters.name: indexNames
parameters.description: Cell array of strings giving named indices, e.g. {'north','south'}.

tools.name: solve
tools.description: Solve a problem-based optimization or equation problem, automatically selecting an appropriate solver and converting the algebraic model to solver form. It returns a solution structure whose fields are named after the optimization variables. Pass an initial point structure for nonlinear problems that need one.
tools.usage:
sol = solve(prob)
sol = solve(prob, x0)
[sol, fval, exitflag, output, lambda] = solve(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: x0
parameters.description: Structure of initial values for nonlinear problems.

parameters.name: 'Solver'
parameters.description: Force a particular solver instead of the automatic choice.

parameters.name: 'Options'
parameters.description: An optimoptions object for the chosen solver.

tools.name: prob2struct
tools.description: Convert a problem-based optimization model into the matrix/function form that a solver-based function expects. Use it to inspect the generated objective and constraint data, to verify a model, or to call the solver directly in a loop for speed. It also writes objective and constraint function files when the model is nonlinear.
tools.usage:
problem = prob2struct(prob)
problem = prob2struct(prob, x0)
problem = prob2struct(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: x0
parameters.description: Initial point structure, required for nonlinear problems.

parameters.name: 'ObjectiveFunctionName'
parameters.description: Name of the generated objective file.

parameters.name: 'FileLocation'
parameters.description: Folder in which to write generated function files.

tools.name: ga
tools.description: Global optimization by a genetic algorithm, evolving a population of candidate solutions through selection, crossover and mutation. It requires no derivatives, handles discontinuous, stochastic and integer-valued objectives, and can escape local minima. It is stochastic, so set rng and use several runs for reproducible results.
tools.usage:
x = ga(fun, nvars)
x = ga(fun, nvars, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
x = ga(fun, nvars, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, intcon, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, population, scores] = ga(___)

parameters.name: intcon
parameters.description: Indices of variables constrained to integers.

parameters.name: 'PopulationSize'
parameters.description: Individuals per generation (default 50, or 200 for more than 5 variables).

parameters.name: 'EliteCount' / 'CrossoverFraction'
parameters.description: How many best individuals survive and the crossover proportion.

parameters.name: 'HybridFcn'
parameters.description: Local solver (e.g. @fmincon) run from the GA's best point to polish it.

tools.name: gamultiobj
tools.description: Find a Pareto front for a multiobjective problem using a controlled elitist genetic algorithm. Rather than a single optimum it returns a set of nondominated solutions spanning the trade-off surface. Use it when objectives genuinely conflict and you want to see the trade-off before deciding.
tools.usage:
x = gamultiobj(fun, nvars)
x = gamultiobj(fun, nvars, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, population, scores] = gamultiobj(___)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Handle returning a VECTOR of objective values.

parameters.name: 'ParetoFraction'
parameters.description: Fraction of the population kept on the Pareto front (default 0.35).

tools.name: particleswarm
tools.description: Global optimization by particle swarm, in which a population of particles flies through the search space guided by their own best and the swarm's best positions. It needs only bounds and a function handle, converges faster than a GA on many continuous problems, and requires no derivatives. Use a HybridFcn to refine the final answer.
tools.usage:
x = particleswarm(fun, nvars)
x = particleswarm(fun, nvars, lb, ub)
x = particleswarm(fun, nvars, lb, ub, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output] = particleswarm(___)

parameters.name: 'HybridFcn'
parameters.description: Local solver run after the swarm converges.

tools.name: simulannealbnd
tools.description: Bounded simulated annealing, which accepts occasional uphill moves with a probability that decreases as the temperature falls. This lets it escape local minima early while converging later. It handles nonsmooth and discontinuous objectives that gradient solvers cannot.
tools.usage:
x = simulannealbnd(fun, x0)
x = simulannealbnd(fun, x0, lb, ub)
x = simulannealbnd(fun, x0, lb, ub, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output] = simulannealbnd(___)

tools.name: patternsearch
tools.description: Direct-search optimization that polls points on a mesh around the current best point, expanding and contracting the mesh as it succeeds or fails. It needs no derivatives, handles nonsmooth objectives and supports linear and nonlinear constraints. Convergence is provably to a stationary point for smooth problems, unlike GA or PSO.
tools.usage:
x = patternsearch(fun, x0)
x = patternsearch(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
x = patternsearch(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output] = patternsearch(___)

parameters.name: 'SearchFcn'
parameters.description: Optional global search step such as @searchlhs or @GPSPositiveBasis2N.

parameters.name: 'MeshTolerance'
parameters.description: Mesh size at which to stop.

parameters.name: 'UseCompletePoll'
parameters.description: Evaluate every poll point instead of stopping at the first improvement.

tools.name: surrogateopt
tools.description: Global optimization designed for objectives that are very expensive to evaluate, such as simulations. It builds a radial-basis surrogate model of the objective, searches that cheap model, and evaluates the true function only at the most promising points. Supports integer variables, bounds and constraints and can be checkpointed and resumed.
tools.usage:
x = surrogateopt(objconstr, lb, ub)
x = surrogateopt(objconstr, lb, ub, intcon)
x = surrogateopt(objconstr, lb, ub, intcon, A, b, Aeq, beq, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, trials] = surrogateopt(___)

parameters.name: objconstr
parameters.description: Handle returning a structure with fields Fval and (optionally) Ineq for nonlinear constraints.

parameters.name: lb, ub
parameters.description: Bounds; both are required and must be finite.

parameters.name: 'MaxFunctionEvaluations'
parameters.description: Evaluation budget, the main cost control.

parameters.name: 'CheckpointFile'
parameters.description: File used to save progress so an interrupted run can resume.

tools.name: GlobalSearch
tools.description: A global solver object that runs fmincon from many trial points generated by a scatter-search algorithm, filtering out points unlikely to improve on the current best. It is designed for smooth problems with multiple local minima where gradient information is still useful. Create the object, create a problem structure with createOptimProblem, then call run.
tools.usage:
gs = GlobalSearch
gs = GlobalSearch(Name, Value)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, solutions] = run(gs, problem)

parameters.name: 'NumTrialPoints'
parameters.description: Number of candidate start points to generate (default 1000).

parameters.name: 'NumStageOnePoints'
parameters.description: Points used in the initial stage (default 200).

parameters.name: 'XTolerance' / 'FunctionTolerance'
parameters.description: Tolerances for deciding that two local solutions are distinct.

tools.name: MultiStart
tools.description: Run a local solver from many start points, either randomly generated or supplied, and collect all distinct local minima found. Unlike GlobalSearch it works with fminunc, lsqnonlin, lsqcurvefit and fmincon, and it can run the starts in parallel. Use it for a straightforward, parallelizable multistart search.
tools.usage:
ms = MultiStart
ms = MultiStart(Name, Value)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, solutions] = run(ms, problem, k)
[___] = run(ms, problem, startpoints)

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Number of randomly generated start points.

parameters.name: 'UseParallel'
parameters.description: Logical; run local solves on a parallel pool.

tools.name: createOptimProblem
tools.description: Build the problem structure that GlobalSearch and MultiStart require, bundling the solver name, objective, start point, bounds, constraints and options. It validates the fields for the chosen local solver. It is the mandatory first step of any GlobalSearch or MultiStart workflow.
tools.usage:
problem = createOptimProblem(solverName)
problem = createOptimProblem(solverName, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'options'
parameters.description: optimoptions object for the local solver.

tools.name: paretosearch
tools.description: Find points on the Pareto front of a multiobjective problem using a direct pattern search, which is usually more accurate and better spread than gamultiobj for smooth problems. It supports bounds, linear constraints and nonlinear constraints. Returns the nondominated design points and their objective values.
tools.usage:
x = paretosearch(fun, nvars)
x = paretosearch(fun, nvars, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output, residuals] = paretosearch(___)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Handle returning a vector of objective values.

parameters.name: 'ParetoSetSize'
parameters.description: Target number of points on the front (default 60).

tools.name: bayesopt
tools.description: Minimize an expensive objective using Bayesian optimization with a Gaussian process surrogate and an acquisition function that balances exploration and exploitation. It handles real, integer and categorical variables and deterministic or noisy objectives. It is the engine behind the 'OptimizeHyperparameters' option of the fit* functions.
tools.usage:
results = bayesopt(fun, vars)
results = bayesopt(fun, vars, Name, Value)

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Handle taking a one-row table of variable values and returning the objective (optionally constraints and user data).

parameters.name: vars
parameters.description: Array of optimizableVariable objects defining ranges, types and transforms.

parameters.name: 'IsObjectiveDeterministic'
parameters.description: Logical; set false for noisy objectives such as cross-validation loss.

tools.name: fminbnd
tools.description: Find the minimum of a single-variable function on a fixed interval using golden-section search and parabolic interpolation. It is derivative-free, guaranteed to stay inside the bracket, and very reliable for unimodal functions. It is part of base MATLAB and needs no toolbox.
tools.usage:
x = fminbnd(fun, x1, x2)
x = fminbnd(fun, x1, x2, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output] = fminbnd(___)

parameters.name: x1, x2
parameters.description: Interval endpoints that bracket the minimum.

tools.notes: Only finds a local minimum inside the bracket; plot the function first if it is multimodal.

tools.name: fzero
tools.description: Find a root of a continuous function of one variable using a combination of bisection, secant and inverse quadratic interpolation. Given a sign-changing interval it is guaranteed to converge. It is part of base MATLAB and is the standard scalar root finder.
tools.usage:
x = fzero(fun, x0)
x = fzero(fun, [x1 x2])
x = fzero(fun, x0, options)
[x, fval, exitflag, output] = fzero(___)

parameters.name: x0
parameters.description: Initial guess, or a two-element interval over which fun changes sign.

tools.notes: Supplying a bracketing interval is much more reliable than a single guess.
